```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";

import Stripe from "stripe";

import { SESSION_APP } from "./checkout";
import {
  HANDLED_EVENTS,
  paymentIntentIdOf,
  sessionOrigin,
  verifyWebhook,
  type CheckoutSessionLike,
  type StripeEventLike,
} from "./webhook-core";

const OPTS = { env: "test", mode: "test" } as const;

/** A session of our app in the test environment; `over` replaces whole properties (an explicit undefined too). */
const own = (over: Partial<CheckoutSessionLike> = {}): CheckoutSessionLike => ({
  id: "cs_test_1",
  mode: "payment",
  metadata: { purchaseId: "p1", app: SESSION_APP, env: "test" },
  ...over,
});

const EVENT: StripeEventLike = {
  id: "evt_1",
  type: "checkout.session.completed",
  livemode: false,
  data: { object: { id: "cs_test_1" } },
};

test("HANDLED_EVENTS: the four checkout events the webhook acts on", () => {
  assert.deepEqual(
    [...HANDLED_EVENTS],
    [
      "checkout.session.completed",
      "checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded",
      "checkout.session.async_payment_failed",
      "checkout.session.expired",
    ],
  );
});

test("paymentIntentIdOf: a string id, an expanded object's id, or null (OUT:32)", () => {
  assert.equal(paymentIntentIdOf("pi_123"), "pi_123");
  assert.equal(paymentIntentIdOf({ id: "pi_456" }), "pi_456");
  assert.equal(paymentIntentIdOf(null), null);
  assert.equal(paymentIntentIdOf(undefined), null);
  assert.equal(paymentIntentIdOf(""), null);
  assert.equal(paymentIntentIdOf({ id: "" }), null);
  assert.equal(paymentIntentIdOf({ id: 5 } as unknown as { id: string }), null);
  assert.equal(paymentIntentIdOf({} as unknown as { id: string }), null);
});

test("verifyWebhook: no signature is missing_signature and the verifier is never called", () => {
  let called = 0;
  const verify = () => {
    called += 1;
    return EVENT;
  };
  assert.deepEqual(verifyWebhook("{}", null, verify), { ok: false, reason: "missing_signature" });
  assert.deepEqual(verifyWebhook("{}", "", verify), { ok: false, reason: "missing_signature" });
  assert.equal(called, 0);
});

test("verifyWebhook: a verifier that throws is bad_signature and nothing of the error is returned", () => {
  const verify = () => {
    throw new Error("No signatures found matching the expected signature for payload sk_live_secret");
  };
  const res = verifyWebhook("{}", "t=1,v1=abc", verify);
  assert.deepEqual(res, { ok: false, reason: "bad_signature" });
});

test("verifyWebhook: a verified event is returned as it is, with the payload and the header the route received", () => {
  const seen: string[] = [];
  const res = verifyWebhook('{"a": 1}', "t=1,v1=abc", (payload, signature) => {
    seen.push(payload, signature);
    return EVENT;
  });
  assert.deepEqual(res, { ok: true, event: EVENT });
  assert.deepEqual(seen, ['{"a": 1}', "t=1,v1=abc"]);
});

// The real verifier, offline (COV-I5): the raw body is the signed message, so a body parsed and re-serialised is refused.
const SECRET = "whsec_offline_test_secret";
const stripe = new Stripe("sk_test_offline");
const verifyReal = (payload: string, signature: string) =>
  stripe.webhooks.constructEvent(payload, signature, SECRET) as unknown as StripeEventLike;
// Pretty-printed on purpose: JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(PAYLOAD)) is a different byte sequence. « séance » is non-ASCII.
const PAYLOAD = JSON.stringify(
  {
    id: "evt_real_1",
    object: "event",
    type: "checkout.session.completed",
    livemode: false,
    data: { object: { id: "cs_test_real", metadata: { note: "séance du lundi" } } },
  },
  null,
  2,
);

test("the real Stripe verifier accepts the exact raw body it was signed on", () => {
  const header = stripe.webhooks.generateTestHeaderString({ payload: PAYLOAD, secret: SECRET });
  const res = verifyWebhook(PAYLOAD, header, verifyReal);
  assert.ok(res.ok);
  assert.equal(res.event.id, "evt_real_1");
  assert.equal(res.event.type, "checkout.session.completed");
});

test("the real Stripe verifier refuses a re-serialised body, one changed byte, another secret and a stale timestamp", () => {
  const header = stripe.webhooks.generateTestHeaderString({ payload: PAYLOAD, secret: SECRET });
  const bad = { ok: false, reason: "bad_signature" };

  const reserialised = JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(PAYLOAD));
  assert.notEqual(reserialised, PAYLOAD, "the fixture really differs once re-serialised");
  assert.deepEqual(verifyWebhook(reserialised, header, verifyReal), bad);

  assert.deepEqual(verifyWebhook(PAYLOAD.replace("séance", "seance"), header, verifyReal), bad);
  assert.deepEqual(verifyWebhook(PAYLOAD.replace("evt_real_1", "evt_real_2"), header, verifyReal), bad);

  const otherSecret = stripe.webhooks.generateTestHeaderString({ payload: PAYLOAD, secret: "whsec_someone_else" });
  assert.deepEqual(verifyWebhook(PAYLOAD, otherSecret, verifyReal), bad);

  assert.deepEqual(verifyWebhook(PAYLOAD, "t=1,v1=deadbeef", verifyReal), bad);
  assert.deepEqual(verifyWebhook(PAYLOAD, "garbage", verifyReal), bad);

  const stale = stripe.webhooks.generateTestHeaderString({
    payload: PAYLOAD,
    secret: SECRET,
    timestamp: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) - 3600,
  });
  assert.deepEqual(verifyWebhook(PAYLOAD, stale, verifyReal), bad, "a replayed old signature is outside the tolerance");
});

test("sessionOrigin: our marker, our environment and the payment mode is own", () => {
  assert.equal(sessionOrigin(own(), OPTS), "own");
  assert.equal(sessionOrigin(own(), { env: "production", mode: "live" }), "other_env");
  assert.equal(
    sessionOrigin(own({ metadata: { purchaseId: "p1", app: SESSION_APP, env: "production" } }), { env: "production", mode: "live" }),
    "own",
  );
});

test("sessionOrigin: our marker with another environment is other_env (SEC-I7)", () => {
  for (const env of ["preview", "production", "development", ""]) {
    assert.equal(sessionOrigin(own({ metadata: { purchaseId: "p1", app: SESSION_APP, env } }), OPTS), "other_env", env);
  }
  assert.equal(sessionOrigin(own({ metadata: { app: SESSION_APP } }), OPTS), "other_env", "no env key at all");
});

test("sessionOrigin: anything without our marker, or not in payment mode, is foreign (SaaS billing, Payment Links)", () => {
  const foreign: [string, CheckoutSessionLike][] = [
    ["no metadata", own({ metadata: null })],
    ["undefined metadata", own({ metadata: undefined })],
    ["empty metadata", own({ metadata: {} })],
    ["purchase id only", own({ metadata: { purchaseId: "p1" } })],
    ["another app", own({ metadata: { app: "someone-else", env: "test" } })],
    ["marker in capitals", own({ metadata: { app: SESSION_APP.toUpperCase(), env: "test" } })],
    ["subscription mode", own({ mode: "subscription" })],
    ["setup mode", own({ mode: "setup" })],
    ["null mode", own({ mode: null })],
    ["missing mode", own({ mode: undefined })],
  ];
  for (const [label, session] of foreign) assert.equal(sessionOrigin(session, OPTS), "foreign", label);
});
```

Create `src/lib/payments/webhook-core.db.test.ts` with exactly this content:

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";

import { eq } from "drizzle-orm";
import { nanoid } from "nanoid";

import { attachCheckoutSession, startBuyAndBook } from "@/lib/booking/claims";
import { startPurchase } from "@/lib/booking/fulfillment";
import type { Db } from "@/lib/db/atomic";
import * as schema from "@/lib/db/schema";
import { SESSION_APP } from "@/lib/payments/checkout";
import {
  handleStripeEvent,
  purchaseOfSession,
  type CheckoutSessionLike,
  type StripeEventLike,
  type WebhookOptions,
  type WebhookOutcome,
} from "@/lib/payments/webhook-core";
import { HEALTH_KEYS, readHealth } from "@/lib/throttle";
import { createTestPro, dbTest, deleteTestUser, type TestPro } from "@/test/db";
import { getBooking, getOccurrence, makeCustomer, makeEvent, makeOffer, makeType, ticketsOf } from "@/test/fixtures";

const TEST: WebhookOptions = { env: "test", mode: "test" };
const LIVE: WebhookOptions = { env: "production", mode: "live" };

/** What every pending purchase of these tests carries: its id, the session attached to it, its price. */
type Base = { purchaseId: string; sessionId: string; amountCents: number; customerId: string };
type BuyBook = Base & { bookingId: string; occurrenceId: string };

async function attach(db: Db, purchaseId: string): Promise<string> {
  const sessionId = `cs_test_${nanoid()}`;
  const attached = await attachCheckoutSession(db, {
    purchaseId,
    checkoutSessionId: sessionId,
    checkoutUrl: `https://checkout.test/${purchaseId}`,
  });
  assert.ok(attached.ok, JSON.stringify(attached));
  return sessionId;
}

/** A buy + book purchase (4 tickets, 85 eur) with its booking held and its session attached, as startBuyAndBookCore leaves it. */
async function pendingBuyBook(db: Db, pro: TestPro): Promise<BuyBook> {
  const typeId = await makeType(db, pro, { name: "Cours collectif" });
  const offerId = await makeOffer(db, pro, typeId, {
    quantity: 4,
    priceCents: 8500,
    validityCount: 3,
    validityUnit: "month",
  });
  const {
    occurrences: [occ],
  } = await makeEvent(db, pro, { ticketTypeIds: [typeId] });
  const customerId = await makeCustomer(db, pro);
  const started = await startBuyAndBook(db, {
    professionalId: pro.proId,
    occurrenceId: occ.id,
    customerId,
    seenStartsAt: occ.startsAt,
    offerId,
  });
  assert.ok(started.ok, JSON.stringify(started));
  const sessionId = await attach(db, started.purchaseId);
  return {
    purchaseId: started.purchaseId,
    sessionId,
    amountCents: started.amountCents,
    customerId,
    bookingId: started.bookingId,
    occurrenceId: occ.id,
  };
}

/** A shop purchase (3 tickets, 190 eur) with its session attached. */
async function pendingShop(db: Db, pro: TestPro): Promise<Base> {
  const typeId = await makeType(db, pro, { name: "Cours collectif" });
  const offerId = await makeOffer(db, pro, typeId, { quantity: 3, priceCents: 19000 });
  const customerId = await makeCustomer(db, pro);
  const started = await startPurchase(db, { professionalId: pro.proId, offerId, customerId });
  assert.ok(started.ok, JSON.stringify(started));
  const sessionId = await attach(db, started.purchaseId);
  return { purchaseId: started.purchaseId, sessionId, amountCents: started.amountCents, customerId };
}

/** The session Stripe would send for `p`: our marker, the purchase id three ways, paid, the exact amount in eur. */
function checkoutSession(p: Pick<Base, "purchaseId" | "sessionId" | "amountCents">, over: Partial<CheckoutSessionLike> = {}, env = TEST.env): CheckoutSessionLike {
  return {
    id: p.sessionId,
    mode: "payment",
    metadata: { purchaseId: p.purchaseId, app: SESSION_APP, env },
    client_reference_id: p.purchaseId,
    payment_status: "paid",
    payment_intent: `pi_test_${nanoid()}`,
    amount_total: p.amountCents,
    currency: "eur",
    ...over,
  };
}

function stripeEvent(type: string, object: unknown, livemode = false): StripeEventLike {
  return { id: `evt_${nanoid()}`, type, livemode, data: { object } };
}

function deliver(db: Db, type: string, object: unknown, opts: WebhookOptions = TEST, livemode = false): Promise<WebhookOutcome> {
  return handleStripeEvent(db, stripeEvent(type, object, livemode), new Date(), opts);
}

const IGNORED: WebhookOutcome = { handled: "ignored", effects: [] };

async function orphans(db: Db): Promise<number> {
  return (await readHealth(db))[HEALTH_KEYS.orphanPayments]?.value ?? 0;
}

async function purchaseRow(db: Db, purchaseId: string) {
  const [row] = await db.select().from(schema.ticketPurchase).where(eq(schema.ticketPurchase.id, purchaseId));
  return row;
}

/** Runs `run` with console.warn / error / info collected into `lines`, restored afterwards. */
async function captureConsole<T>(run: () => Promise<T>): Promise<{ result: T; lines: string[] }> {
  const lines: string[] = [];
  const saved = { warn: console.warn, error: console.error, info: console.info };
  const take = (...args: unknown[]) => {
    lines.push(args.map(String).join(" "));
  };
  console.warn = take;
  console.error = take;
  console.info = take;
  try {
    return { result: await run(), lines };
  } finally {
    console.warn = saved.warn;
    console.error = saved.error;
    console.info = saved.info;
  }
}

dbTest("E10 completed + paid fulfils a buy + book: tickets, confirmed booking, receipt + confirmation + pro notice + sync", async ({ db, pro }) => {
  const p = await pendingBuyBook(db, pro);
  const pi = `pi_test_${nanoid()}`;

  const out = await deliver(db, "checkout.session.completed", checkoutSession(p, { payment_intent: pi }));
  assert.equal(out.handled, "fulfilled");
  assert.deepEqual(out.effects, [
    { type: "email.purchase_receipt", purchaseId: p.purchaseId },
    { type: "email.booking_confirmed", bookingId: p.bookingId },
    { type: "email.pro_new_booking", bookingId: p.bookingId },
    { type: "google.sync_occurrence", occurrenceId: p.occurrenceId },
  ]);

  const row = await purchaseRow(db, p.purchaseId);
  assert.equal(row.status, "paid");
  assert.equal(row.livemode, false);
  assert.equal(row.paymentIntentId, pi);
  assert.equal(row.checkoutSessionId, p.sessionId);
  assert.equal((await getBooking(db, p.bookingId)).status, "confirmed");
  assert.equal((await getOccurrence(db, p.occurrenceId)).seatsTaken, 1);
  const tickets = await ticketsOf(db, p.customerId);
  assert.equal(tickets.length, 4);
  assert.equal(tickets.filter((t) => t.status === "booked").length, 1);
});

dbTest("E10 the same completed event twice is a duplicate: no second ticket, no second e-mail (S12)", async ({ db, pro }) => {
  const p = await pendingShop(db, pro);
  const event = stripeEvent("checkout.session.completed", checkoutSession(p));
  const before = await orphans(db);

  const first = await handleStripeEvent(db, event, new Date(), TEST);
  assert.equal(first.handled, "fulfilled");
  assert.deepEqual(first.effects, [{ type: "email.purchase_receipt", purchaseId: p.purchaseId }]);

  const again = await handleStripeEvent(db, event, new Date(), TEST);
  assert.deepEqual(again, { handled: "duplicate", effects: [] });
  assert.equal((await ticketsOf(db, p.customerId)).length, 3, "the tickets were issued once");
  assert.equal(await orphans(db), before, "a retry of the same payment is not an orphan");
});

dbTest("E10 a second payment of a paid purchase is an orphan: counted for a refund, no new ticket (SEC-M2)", async ({ db, pro }) => {
  const p = await pendingShop(db, pro);
  assert.equal((await deliver(db, "checkout.session.completed", checkoutSession(p))).handled, "fulfilled");
  const before = await orphans(db);

  // Another Checkout session of the same purchase, paid with another payment intent.
  const second = { ...p, sessionId: `cs_test_${nanoid()}` };
  const out = await deliver(db, "checkout.session.completed", checkoutSession(second));
  assert.deepEqual(out, { handled: "orphan", effects: [] });
  assert.equal(await orphans(db), before + 1);
  assert.equal((await ticketsOf(db, p.customerId)).length, 3, "no ticket for the second payment");
  assert.equal((await purchaseRow(db, p.purchaseId)).checkoutSessionId, p.sessionId, "the first payment stays the purchase's");
});

dbTest("E10 completed + unpaid marks processing (delayed method), then async_payment_succeeded fulfils", async ({ db, pro }) => {
  const p = await pendingShop(db, pro);
  const pi = `pi_test_${nanoid()}`;

  const unpaid = await deliver(db, "checkout.session.completed", checkoutSession(p, { payment_status: "unpaid", payment_intent: pi }));
  assert.deepEqual(unpaid, { handled: "processing", effects: [] });
  const waiting = await purchaseRow(db, p.purchaseId);
  assert.equal(waiting.status, "pending");
  assert.ok(waiting.processingAt, "processing_at is set");
  assert.equal((await ticketsOf(db, p.customerId)).length, 0);

  const paid = await deliver(db, "checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded", checkoutSession(p, { payment_intent: pi }));
  assert.equal(paid.handled, "fulfilled");
  assert.deepEqual(paid.effects, [{ type: "email.purchase_receipt", purchaseId: p.purchaseId }]);
  assert.equal((await ticketsOf(db, p.customerId)).length, 3);

  // An unpaid event arriving after the payment cannot take the purchase back to processing.
  const late = await deliver(db, "checkout.session.completed", checkoutSession(p, { payment_status: "unpaid", payment_intent: pi }));
  assert.deepEqual(late, IGNORED);
  assert.equal((await purchaseRow(db, p.purchaseId)).status, "paid");
});

dbTest("E11 async_payment_failed releases the hold: purchase and booking expired, seat freed, Google re-synced", async ({ db, pro }) => {
  const p = await pendingBuyBook(db, pro);
  const out = await deliver(db, "checkout.session.async_payment_failed", checkoutSession(p, { payment_status: "unpaid" }));
  assert.deepEqual(out, {
    handled: "released",
    effects: [{ type: "google.sync_occurrence", occurrenceId: p.occurrenceId }],
  });
  assert.equal((await purchaseRow(db, p.purchaseId)).status, "expired");
  assert.equal((await getBooking(db, p.bookingId)).status, "expired");
  assert.equal((await getOccurrence(db, p.occurrenceId)).seatsTaken, 0);
});

  const p = await pendingBuyBook(db, pro);

  assert.deepEqual(shopOut, { handled: "released", effects: [] });

});

    await deleteTestUser(db, other.userId);

  }
});

  assert.equal((await deliver(db, "checkout.session.completed", noMetadataId)).handled, "fulfilled");
  assert.equal((await ticketsOf(db, bare.customerId)).length, 3);

  const stale = await pendingShop(db, pro);
  const unknownMetadataId = checkoutSession(stale, { metadata: { purchaseId: nanoid(), app: SESSION_APP, env: TEST.env } });
  assert.equal((await deliver(db, "checkout.session.completed", unknownMetadataId)).handled, "fulfilled");
  assert.equal((await ticketsOf(db, stale.customerId)).length, 3);
});

dbTest("E10 a paid session of ours with no purchase to settle is an orphan: 200 and counted for a manual refund", async ({ db }) => {

});

dbTest("E10 an amount or a currency that is not the purchase's issues nothing and is an orphan (SEC-M1, S39)", async ({ db, pro }) => {
  const p = await pendingShop(db, pro);
  const before = await orphans(db);

  const wrong: [string, Partial<CheckoutSessionLike>][] = [
    ["one cent more", { amount_total: p.amountCents + 1 }],
    ["one cent less", { amount_total: p.amountCents - 1 }],
    ["no amount", { amount_total: null }],
    ["another currency", { currency: "usd" }],
    ["no currency", { currency: null }],
  ];
  for (const [label, over] of wrong) {
    const out = await deliver(db, "checkout.session.completed", checkoutSession(p, over));
    assert.deepEqual(out, { handled: "orphan", effects: [] }, label);
  }
  assert.equal(await orphans(db), before + wrong.length);
  assert.equal((await purchaseRow(db, p.purchaseId)).status, "pending", "the purchase is still waiting for its real payment");
  assert.equal((await ticketsOf(db, p.customerId)).length, 0);

  // The right amount in capitals (Stripe sends lower case, the comparison is case-insensitive) settles it.
  const ok = await deliver(db, "checkout.session.completed", checkoutSession(p, { currency: "EUR" }));
  assert.equal(ok.handled, "fulfilled");
  assert.equal((await ticketsOf(db, p.customerId)).length, 3);
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create `src/lib/payments/webhook-core.ts`**

```ts
/**
 * The Stripe event handler on the tickets engine (spec E10, E11, L1106-1143,
 * contract § 3.12). Pure of Next and of the Stripe SDK: the route passes
 * stripe.webhooks.constructEvent in as a function and hands over the db, so
 * every rule below is tested without a network. Only sessions of OUR app in
 * OUR environment are acted on (SEC-I7): the Stripe account also receives the
 * SaaS billing, Payment Links and the events of other deployments, none of
 * which is ever an orphan to refund. Idempotency is the engine's.
 */
import { eq } from "drizzle-orm";

import { fulfillPurchase, markProcessing, recordOrphanPayment, type PaymentFacts } from "@/lib/booking/fulfillment";
import { releasePurchase } from "@/lib/booking/release";
import type { Effect } from "@/lib/booking/types";
import type { Db } from "@/lib/db/atomic";
import { ticketPurchase } from "@/lib/db/schema";
import { SESSION_APP, type PaymentMode } from "@/lib/payments/checkout";
import { idSchema } from "@/lib/tickets";

export type CheckoutSessionLike = {
  id: string;
  mode?: string | null;
  metadata?: Record<string, string> | null;
  client_reference_id?: string | null;
  payment_status?: string | null;
  payment_intent?: string | { id: string } | null;
  amount_total?: number | null;
  currency?: string | null;
};

export type StripeEventLike = { id: string; type: string; livemode: boolean; data: { object: unknown } };

export type WebhookHandled = "fulfilled" | "duplicate" | "orphan" | "processing" | "released" | "ignored";
export type WebhookOutcome = { handled: WebhookHandled; effects: Effect[] };

/** The deployment the handler runs in (SEC-I7, SEC-M1): env = APP_ENV, mode = paymentMode(). */
export type WebhookOptions = { env: string; mode: PaymentMode };

export const HANDLED_EVENTS = [
  "checkout.session.completed",
  "checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded",
  "checkout.session.async_payment_failed",
  "checkout.session.expired",
] as const;
type HandledEvent = (typeof HANDLED_EVENTS)[number];

function isHandled(type: string): type is HandledEvent {
  return (HANDLED_EVENTS as readonly string[]).includes(type);
}

/** A string id, an expanded object's id, or null (OUT:32). */
export function paymentIntentIdOf(pi: CheckoutSessionLike["payment_intent"]): string | null {
  if (typeof pi === "string") return pi === "" ? null : pi;
  if (typeof pi === "object" && pi !== null && typeof pi.id === "string" && pi.id !== "") return pi.id;
  return null;
}

/** SEC-I7: "own" = mode "payment", metadata.app === SESSION_APP and metadata.env === opts.env; "other_env" = our marker with another env; "foreign" = anything else (SaaS billing, Payment Links, other apps on the account). */
export function sessionOrigin(session: CheckoutSessionLike, opts: WebhookOptions): "own" | "other_env" | "foreign" {
  if (session.mode !== "payment") return "foreign";
  const meta = session.metadata;
  if (!meta || meta.app !== SESSION_APP) return "foreign";
  return meta.env === opts.env ? "own" : "other_env";
}

export type SessionPurchase = { kind: "found"; purchaseId: string } | { kind: "none" } | { kind: "mismatch" };

/** metadata.purchaseId (idSchema) of an existing purchase, else the purchase whose checkout_session_id = session.id (UNIQUE); a set client_reference_id that differs from the found id → mismatch (it is only a consistency check, SEC-I7). */
export async function purchaseOfSession(db: Db, session: CheckoutSessionLike): Promise<SessionPurchase> {
  let purchaseId: string | null = null;
  const fromMetadata = idSchema.safeParse(session.metadata?.purchaseId);
  if (fromMetadata.success) {
    const [row] = await db.select({ id: ticketPurchase.id }).from(ticketPurchase).where(eq(ticketPurchase.id, fromMetadata.data));
    purchaseId = row?.id ?? null;
  }
  if (purchaseId === null) {
    const [row] = await db
      .select({ id: ticketPurchase.id })
      .from(ticketPurchase)
      .where(eq(ticketPurchase.checkoutSessionId, session.id));
    purchaseId = row?.id ?? null;
  }
  if (purchaseId === null) return { kind: "none" };
  const reference = session.client_reference_id;
  if (typeof reference === "string" && reference !== "" && reference !== purchaseId) return { kind: "mismatch" };
  return { kind: "found", purchaseId };
}

export type VerifiedWebhook =
  | { ok: true; event: StripeEventLike }
  | { ok: false; reason: "missing_signature" | "bad_signature" };

/** Pure: no signature → missing; `verify` throwing → bad (the route passes stripe.webhooks.constructEvent bound to the secret). */
export function verifyWebhook(
  payload: string,
  signature: string | null,
  verify: (payload: string, signature: string) => StripeEventLike,
): VerifiedWebhook {
  if (!signature) return { ok: false, reason: "missing_signature" };
  try {
    return { ok: true, event: verify(payload, signature) };
  } catch {
    return { ok: false, reason: "bad_signature" };
  }
}

const ignored = (): WebhookOutcome => ({ handled: "ignored", effects: [] });

/** The object of an event when it looks like a session: a non-null object with a non-empty string id. */
function sessionOf(object: unknown): CheckoutSessionLike | null {
  if (typeof object !== "object" || object === null) return null;
  const id = (object as { id?: unknown }).id;
  return typeof id === "string" && id !== "" ? (object as CheckoutSessionLike) : null;
}

/** Money for a session that cannot be settled (no purchase, wrong amount): counted and logged by the engine, refunded by hand. */
async function orphan(db: Db, facts: PaymentFacts, now: Date): Promise<WebhookOutcome> {
  await recordOrphanPayment(db, facts, now);
  return { handled: "orphan", effects: [] };
}

/** Rule 5: a paid session settles its purchase, or is an orphan. */
async function fulfil(
  db: Db,
  found: SessionPurchase,
  session: CheckoutSessionLike,
  facts: PaymentFacts,
  now: Date,
): Promise<WebhookOutcome> {
  if (found.kind !== "found") return orphan(db, facts, now);

  const [snapshot] = await db
    .select({ amountCents: ticketPurchase.amountCents, currency: ticketPurchase.currency })
    .from(ticketPurchase)
    .where(eq(ticketPurchase.id, found.purchaseId));
  if (!snapshot) return orphan(db, facts, now);
  if (
    session.amount_total !== snapshot.amountCents ||
    (session.currency ?? "").toLowerCase() !== snapshot.currency.toLowerCase()
  ) {
    const settled = await orphan(db, facts, now);
    console.error("[stripe] amount mismatch on a purchase");
    return settled;
  }

  const res = await fulfillPurchase(db, found.purchaseId, facts, now);
  if (res.outcome === "duplicate") {
    // Read after the engine answered: two identical concurrent deliveries (one wins, one is the duplicate) store the same ids.
    const [stored] = await db
      .select({ paymentIntentId: ticketPurchase.paymentIntentId, checkoutSessionId: ticketPurchase.checkoutSessionId })
      .from(ticketPurchase)
      .where(eq(ticketPurchase.id, found.purchaseId));
    if (!stored) return orphan(db, facts, now);
    const otherPayment = stored.paymentIntentId !== null && stored.paymentIntentId !== facts.paymentIntentId;
    const otherSession = stored.checkoutSessionId !== null && stored.checkoutSessionId !== facts.sessionId;
    if (otherPayment || otherSession) return orphan(db, facts, now);
  }
  return { handled: res.outcome, effects: res.effects };
}

/** Rule 7: `async_payment_failed` and `expired` release the purchase of THIS session only. */
async function release(
  db: Db,
  found: SessionPurchase,
  session: CheckoutSessionLike,
  type: string,
  now: Date,
): Promise<WebhookOutcome> {
  // The common case of LED:427: the pro was deleted, its open sessions expire, their purchases no longer exist.
  if (found.kind !== "found") return ignored();
  const [row] = await db
    .select({ checkoutSessionId: ticketPurchase.checkoutSessionId })
    .from(ticketPurchase)
    .where(eq(ticketPurchase.id, found.purchaseId));
  if (!row) return ignored();
  if (row.checkoutSessionId !== null && row.checkoutSessionId !== session.id) {
    console.warn(`[stripe] ${type} ignored: not the purchase's session`);
    return ignored();
  }
  const res = await releasePurchase(db, found.purchaseId, now);
  if (res.ok) return { handled: "released", effects: res.effects };
  if (res.code === "not_found") return ignored();
  throw new Error(`releasePurchase ${found.purchaseId}: unexpected ${res.code}`);
}

/** E10 / E11 dispatch (rules below). Idempotent through the engine; throws on an unexpected error (the route answers 500 and Stripe retries). */
export async function handleStripeEvent(
  db: Db,
  event: StripeEventLike,
  now: Date,
  opts: WebhookOptions,
): Promise<WebhookOutcome> {
  const type = event.type;
  if (!isHandled(type)) return ignored();
  const session = sessionOf(event.data?.object);
  if (!session) return ignored();

  if (event.livemode !== (opts.mode === "live")) {
    console.warn(`[stripe] ${type} ignored: livemode mismatch`);
    return ignored();
  }
  const origin = sessionOrigin(session, opts);
  if (origin === "foreign") return ignored();
  if (origin === "other_env") {
    console.warn(`[stripe] ${type} ignored: other environment`);
    return ignored();
  }

  const facts: PaymentFacts = {
    sessionId: session.id,
    paymentIntentId: paymentIntentIdOf(session.payment_intent),
    livemode: event.livemode,
  };
  const found = await purchaseOfSession(db, session);
  if (found.kind === "mismatch") {
    console.warn(`[stripe] ${type} ignored: reference mismatch`);
    return ignored();
  }

  switch (type) {
    case "checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded":
      return fulfil(db, found, session, facts, now);
    case "checkout.session.completed": {
      if (session.payment_status === "paid") return fulfil(db, found, session, facts, now);
      if (session.payment_status === "no_payment_required") {
        console.warn("[stripe] no_payment_required ignored");
        return ignored();
      }
      if (session.payment_status === "unpaid" && found.kind === "found") {
        const res = await markProcessing(db, found.purchaseId, now);
        return res.ok ? { handled: "processing", effects: [] } : ignored();
      }
      return ignored();
    }
    case "checkout.session.async_payment_failed":
    case "checkout.session.expired":
      return release(db, found, session, type, now);
  }
}
```

Replace the whole content of `src/app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts` (Write) with:

```ts
import { after } from "next/server";

import { db } from "@/lib/db";
import { env } from "@/lib/env";
import { logSafeMessage } from "@/lib/log-safe";
import { handleStripeEvent, verifyWebhook, type StripeEventLike, type WebhookOutcome } from "@/lib/payments/webhook-core";
import { paymentMode, stripe } from "@/lib/stripe";
import { runEffects } from "@/server/notify";

export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";

const NO_STORE = { "Cache-Control": "no-store" } as const;

function reply(body: string, status: number): Response {
  return new Response(body, { status, headers: NO_STORE });
}

/**
 * Stripe webhook (spec E10, E11, contract § 3.12). Stripe off: 404. Stripe on
 * without its signing secret: 500 and one log line (Stripe keeps retrying
 * while the owner fixes it, never a silent 200). The signature is checked on
 * the RAW body, so the body is read as text and never parsed first. A bad or
 * missing signature: 400 and the reason only. The event goes to the tested
 * handler with the deployment's environment and payment mode; an unexpected
 * throw is a 500 (Stripe retries), logged through logSafeMessage, never as a
 * raw error object. Every other outcome, `ignored` and `orphan` included, is a
 * 200. The effects (receipt, confirmation or late-payment notice, the pro's
 * notice, Google) run after the response with the budget "none": they are the
 * client's due and never count against a pro (Decision 74).
 */
export async function POST(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  const client = stripe;
  if (!env.STRIPE_ENABLED || !client) return reply("Not found", 404);
  const secret = env.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET;
  if (!env.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_CONFIGURED || !secret) {
    console.error("[stripe] webhook secret missing");
    return reply("Webhook not configured", 500);
  }

  const payload = await request.text();
  const verified = verifyWebhook(
    payload,
    request.headers.get("stripe-signature"),
    (body, signature) => client.webhooks.constructEvent(body, signature, secret) as unknown as StripeEventLike,
  );
  if (!verified.ok) {
    console.warn(`[stripe] signature rejected: ${verified.reason}`);
    return reply("Invalid signature", 400);
  }
  const { event } = verified;

  let outcome: WebhookOutcome;
  try {
    outcome = await handleStripeEvent(db, event, new Date(), { env: env.APP_ENV, mode: paymentMode() });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(`[stripe] ${event.type} failed: ${logSafeMessage(err)}`);
    return reply("Error", 500);
  }

  const effects = outcome.effects;
  if (effects.length > 0) after(() => runEffects(effects, "none"));
  return reply("ok", 200);
}
```

```ts
// src/lib/same-origin.ts (pure)
/** Origin header equals new URL(appUrl).origin (route handlers get no automatic origin check); null, "null" or a malformed appUrl → false. */
export function sameOrigin(originHeader: string | null, appUrl: string): boolean;

// src/lib/payments/mock-checkout.ts (DB + pure; no server-only)
export type MockCheckoutView = { purchaseId: string; businessName: string; productLabel: string; amountLabel: string; cancelPath: string };
export async function mockCheckoutState(db: Db, purchaseId: string): Promise<{ kind: "pending"; view: MockCheckoutView } | { kind: "paid"; merciPath: string } | null>;
export type MockPayResult = { kind: "paid"; merciPath: string; effects: Effect[] } | { kind: "not_found" };
export async function mockPay(db: Db, purchaseId: string, now: Date): Promise<MockPayResult>;
export function mockCheckoutHtml(view: MockCheckoutView): string;
// addition of this task (not in § 3.13): the cancel link rule, exported so its three branches are unit tested
export function mockCancelPath(p: { slug: string; purchaseId: string; occurrenceId: string | null; offerId: string | null }): string;

// src/app/api/mock-checkout/route.ts
export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";
export async function GET(request: Request): Promise<Response>;
export async function POST(request: Request): Promise<Response>;
```

Design notes (read before coding):
- The simulated checkout is the P2 stand-in for Stripe Checkout in mock mode. It exists only when `mockCheckoutEnabled()` (no Stripe keys, not production by `APP_ENV` nor by `VERCEL_ENV`, one rule, SEC-I5): everywhere else the route answers 404 to both verbs.
- A GET writes nothing (spec L1847: link scanners and prefetchers open URLs): it shows the page. Paying is a same-origin POST. Neither takes a redirect parameter (L1146-1147): the target is `/{slug of the purchase's own pro}/merci?p={id}` built from the database and `env.APP_URL`.
- The mock pays only SIMULATED sessions (SEC-M3): a purchase whose `checkout_session_id` is null or `mock_<id>`. A purchase opened against Stripe (`cs_...`) is never shown and never paid here, whether it is pending or paid. This is stricter than the contract's « a paid one → its merci path » for a paid purchase attached to a Stripe session, which answers null here.
- `mockPay` answers `not_found` when the engine says `orphan` (the purchase vanished between the read and the batch): the simulation never bumps the admin's orphan counter for a purchase it did not find first.
- `mockPay` also pays a simulated purchase that has already expired (a stale tab): money always yields tickets (E10), and this is how the late-payment e-mail is exercised in mock mode.
- Deviation noted: `isReferenceId` (Task 12) guards the id of the GET query and of the POST form, and `mockCancelPath` is exported for its test.

**Security tests owned here (contract § 8.4):**
- S15 (mock part): `same-origin.test.ts` (other host, scheme, port, `null`, `"null"`, appUrl with a trailing slash or a path); `mock-checkout.db.test.ts` (`mockCheckoutState` writes nothing); `mock-checkout.test.ts` route guard (GET holds no write, `mockCheckoutEnabled()` first in both verbs, same-origin before the POST body is read).
- S40: `mock-checkout.db.test.ts` (a purchase attached to `cs_test_...`: state null, pay `not_found`, nothing paid).
- S47 (mock part): `mock-checkout.test.ts` route guard (the four response headers) and the `curl -sI` check of the browser step.
- S49 (mock route): `mock-checkout.test.ts` route guard (`runEffects(effects, "none")`).
- S6: `mock-checkout.db.test.ts` (another pro's purchase pays and redirects within its own pro; the first pro is untouched).
- S31 (mock route): `mock-checkout.test.ts` route guard (no raw `err` passed to `console.*`).

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";

import { sameOrigin } from "./same-origin";

const APP = "https://myskedul.com";

test("sameOrigin: the app's own origin is accepted, whatever the shape of the configured URL", () => {
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("https://myskedul.com", APP), true);
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("https://myskedul.com", "https://myskedul.com/"), true, "trailing slash");
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("https://myskedul.com", "https://myskedul.com/app/x?y=1"), true, "path and query");
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("https://myskedul.com", "https://myskedul.com:443"), true, "default port");
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("http://localhost:3102", "http://localhost:3102"), true, "the dev server");
});

test("sameOrigin: another host, a subdomain or a lookalike is refused", () => {
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("https://evil.example", APP), false);
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("https://www.myskedul.com", APP), false);
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("https://myskedul.com.evil.example", APP), false);
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("https://evilmyskedul.com", APP), false);
});

test("sameOrigin: another scheme or another port is refused", () => {
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("http://myskedul.com", APP), false);
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("https://myskedul.com:8443", APP), false);
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("http://localhost:3000", "http://localhost:3102"), false);
});

test("sameOrigin: no header, the opaque origin and anything that is not an origin are refused", () => {
  assert.equal(sameOrigin(null, APP), false);
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("null", APP), false);
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("", APP), false);
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("https://myskedul.com/", APP), false, "an Origin header never ends with a slash");
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("https://myskedul.com/path", APP), false);
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("HTTPS://MYSKEDUL.COM", APP), false, "browsers send the lower-case serialisation");
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("myskedul.com", APP), false);
});

test("sameOrigin: a malformed or opaque configured URL accepts nothing", () => {
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("https://myskedul.com", "not a url"), false);
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("https://myskedul.com", ""), false);
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("https://myskedul.com", "myskedul.com"), false);
  assert.equal(sameOrigin("null", "data:,x"), false, "an opaque app URL has the origin \"null\", which is never a match");
});
```

```ts
  assert.ok(html.includes('<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">'));
```

```ts
import type { Db } from "@/lib/db/atomic";

import { mockSessionId } from "@/lib/payments/checkout";
import { mockCheckoutState, mockPay } from "@/lib/payments/mock-checkout";
import { HEALTH_KEYS, readHealth } from "@/lib/throttle";
import { formatMoney } from "@/lib/utils";
import { createTestPro, dbTest, deleteTestUser, type TestPro } from "@/test/db";
import { getBooking, getOccurrence, makeCustomer, makeEvent, makeOffer, makeType, ticketsOf } from "@/test/fixtures";

type Session = "mock" | "none" | "stripe";

/** Attaches the session of `kind` to the purchase, the way the action leaves it (`none` leaves the purchase unattached). */
async function attach(db: Db, purchaseId: string, kind: Session): Promise<string | null> {
  if (kind === "none") return null;
  const sessionId = kind === "mock" ? mockSessionId(purchaseId) : `cs_test_${nanoid()}`;
  const attached = await attachCheckoutSession(db, {
    purchaseId,
    checkoutSessionId: sessionId,
    checkoutUrl: `https://checkout.test/${purchaseId}`,
  });
  assert.ok(attached.ok, JSON.stringify(attached));
  return sessionId;
}

/** A buy + book purchase of « Altinha débutants » (4 tickets, 85 eur) with its booking held. */
async function buyBook(db: Db, pro: TestPro, kind: Session = "mock") {
  const typeId = await makeType(db, pro, { name: "Cours collectif" });
  const offerId = await makeOffer(db, pro, typeId, {
    quantity: 4,
    priceCents: 8500,
    validityCount: 3,
    validityUnit: "month",
  });
  const {
    occurrences: [occ],
  } = await makeEvent(db, pro, { title: "Altinha débutants", ticketTypeIds: [typeId] });
  const customerId = await makeCustomer(db, pro);
  const started = await startBuyAndBook(db, {
    professionalId: pro.proId,
    occurrenceId: occ.id,
    customerId,
    seenStartsAt: occ.startsAt,
    offerId,
  });
  assert.ok(started.ok, JSON.stringify(started));
  const sessionId = await attach(db, started.purchaseId, kind);
  return { purchaseId: started.purchaseId, bookingId: started.bookingId, occurrenceId: occ.id, offerId, customerId, sessionId };
}

/** A shop purchase of the 3-ticket offer (190 eur). */
async function shop(db: Db, pro: TestPro, kind: Session = "mock") {
  const typeId = await makeType(db, pro, { name: "Cours collectif" });
  const offerId = await makeOffer(db, pro, typeId, { quantity: 3, priceCents: 19000 });
  const customerId = await makeCustomer(db, pro);
  const started = await startPurchase(db, { professionalId: pro.proId, offerId, customerId });
  assert.ok(started.ok, JSON.stringify(started));
  const sessionId = await attach(db, started.purchaseId, kind);
  return { purchaseId: started.purchaseId, offerId, customerId, sessionId };
}

async function purchaseRow(db: Db, purchaseId: string) {
  const [row] = await db.select().from(schema.ticketPurchase).where(eq(schema.ticketPurchase.id, purchaseId));
  return row;
}

async function businessNameOf(db: Db, pro: TestPro): Promise<string> {
  const [row] = await db
    .select({ businessName: schema.professional.businessName })
    .from(schema.professional)
    .where(eq(schema.professional.id, pro.proId));
  return row.businessName;
}

const orphans = async (db: Db): Promise<number> => (await readHealth(db))[HEALTH_KEYS.orphanPayments]?.value ?? 0;

dbTest("mockCheckoutState: a pending simulated purchase shows its view, the cancel link goes back to the séance or the offer", async ({ db, pro }) => {
  const businessName = await businessNameOf(db, pro);

  const b = await buyBook(db, pro);
  assert.deepEqual(await mockCheckoutState(db, b.purchaseId), {
    kind: "pending",
    view: {
      purchaseId: b.purchaseId,
      businessName,
      productLabel: "Altinha débutants · Carnet de 4",
      amountLabel: formatMoney(8500, "eur"),
      cancelPath: `/${pro.slug}/seance/${b.occurrenceId}?paiement=annule&p=${b.purchaseId}`,
    },
  });

  const s = await shop(db, pro);
  assert.deepEqual(await mockCheckoutState(db, s.purchaseId), {
    kind: "pending",
    view: {
      purchaseId: s.purchaseId,
      businessName,
      productLabel: "Cours collectif · Carnet de 3",
      amountLabel: formatMoney(19000, "eur"),
      cancelPath: `/${pro.slug}/offre/${s.offerId}?paiement=annule&p=${s.purchaseId}`,
    },
  });

  // A purchase with no session attached yet (the window between the engine and the gateway) is simulated too.
  const unattached = await shop(db, pro, "none");
  assert.equal((await mockCheckoutState(db, unattached.purchaseId))?.kind, "pending");
});

dbTest("mockCheckoutState writes nothing: a GET is safe for prefetchers and link scanners (S15)", async ({ db, pro }) => {
  const b = await buyBook(db, pro);
  const snapshot = async () => ({
    purchase: await purchaseRow(db, b.purchaseId),
    booking: await getBooking(db, b.bookingId),
    occurrence: await getOccurrence(db, b.occurrenceId),
    tickets: (await ticketsOf(db, b.customerId)).length,
    orphans: await orphans(db),
  });
  const before = await snapshot();
  assert.equal((await mockCheckoutState(db, b.purchaseId))?.kind, "pending");
  assert.equal((await mockCheckoutState(db, b.purchaseId))?.kind, "pending");
  assert.deepEqual(await snapshot(), before);
  assert.equal(before.purchase.status, "pending");
});

dbTest("mockPay: a simulated buy + book is fulfilled with livemode false, the booking is confirmed, the merci path is the pro's own", async ({ db, pro }) => {
  const b = await buyBook(db, pro);
  const res = await mockPay(db, b.purchaseId, new Date());
  assert.deepEqual(res, {
    kind: "paid",
    merciPath: `/${pro.slug}/merci?p=${b.purchaseId}`,
    effects: [
      { type: "email.purchase_receipt", purchaseId: b.purchaseId },
      { type: "email.booking_confirmed", bookingId: b.bookingId },
      { type: "email.pro_new_booking", bookingId: b.bookingId },
      { type: "google.sync_occurrence", occurrenceId: b.occurrenceId },
    ],
  });
  const row = await purchaseRow(db, b.purchaseId);
  assert.equal(row.status, "paid");
  assert.equal(row.livemode, false);
  assert.equal(row.paymentIntentId, null);
  assert.equal(row.checkoutSessionId, mockSessionId(b.purchaseId), "the simulated session id stays");
  assert.equal((await getBooking(db, b.bookingId)).status, "confirmed");
  const tickets = await ticketsOf(db, b.customerId);
  assert.equal(tickets.length, 4);
  assert.equal(tickets.filter((t) => t.status === "booked").length, 1);

  // The page of a paid purchase sends the visitor to the merci page.
  assert.deepEqual(await mockCheckoutState(db, b.purchaseId), { kind: "paid", merciPath: `/${pro.slug}/merci?p=${b.purchaseId}` });

  // A second click, or a double submit: the same path, no effect, no new ticket.
  assert.deepEqual(await mockPay(db, b.purchaseId, new Date()), {
    kind: "paid",
    merciPath: `/${pro.slug}/merci?p=${b.purchaseId}`,
    effects: [],
  });
  assert.equal((await ticketsOf(db, b.customerId)).length, 4);
});

dbTest("mockPay: a shop purchase with no session attached is simulated too and keeps its session null", async ({ db, pro }) => {
  const s = await shop(db, pro, "none");
  const res = await mockPay(db, s.purchaseId, new Date());
  assert.deepEqual(res, {
    kind: "paid",
    merciPath: `/${pro.slug}/merci?p=${s.purchaseId}`,
    effects: [{ type: "email.purchase_receipt", purchaseId: s.purchaseId }],
  });
  const row = await purchaseRow(db, s.purchaseId);
  assert.equal(row.status, "paid");
  assert.equal(row.checkoutSessionId, null);
  assert.equal((await ticketsOf(db, s.customerId)).length, 3);
});

dbTest("SEC-M3 the mock pays only simulated sessions: a purchase opened against Stripe is neither shown nor paid (S40)", async ({ db, pro }) => {
  const b = await buyBook(db, pro, "stripe");
  assert.equal(await mockCheckoutState(db, b.purchaseId), null);
  assert.deepEqual(await mockPay(db, b.purchaseId, new Date()), { kind: "not_found" });
  assert.equal((await purchaseRow(db, b.purchaseId)).status, "pending");
  assert.equal((await getBooking(db, b.bookingId)).status, "pending");
  assert.equal((await getOccurrence(db, b.occurrenceId)).seatsTaken, 1);
  assert.equal((await ticketsOf(db, b.customerId)).length, 0);

  // Once Stripe has paid it, the mock still knows nothing of it (no merci redirect for a Stripe payment).
  const s = await shop(db, pro, "stripe");
  await fulfillPurchase(db, s.purchaseId, { sessionId: s.sessionId, paymentIntentId: `pi_test_${nanoid()}`, livemode: false });
  assert.equal(await mockCheckoutState(db, s.purchaseId), null);
  assert.deepEqual(await mockPay(db, s.purchaseId, new Date()), { kind: "not_found" });
  assert.equal((await ticketsOf(db, s.customerId)).length, 3, "no second set of tickets");
});

dbTest("mockPay on a simulated purchase whose hold was released: tickets and a late-payment notice, the booking stays expired", async ({ db, pro }) => {
  const b = await buyBook(db, pro);
  const released = await releasePurchase(db, b.purchaseId, new Date());
  assert.ok(released.ok, JSON.stringify(released));
  assert.equal(await mockCheckoutState(db, b.purchaseId), null, "an expired purchase shows no page");

  const res = await mockPay(db, b.purchaseId, new Date());
  assert.deepEqual(res, {
    kind: "paid",
    merciPath: `/${pro.slug}/merci?p=${b.purchaseId}`,
    effects: [
      { type: "email.purchase_receipt", purchaseId: b.purchaseId },
      { type: "email.late_payment", purchaseId: b.purchaseId },
    ],
  });
  assert.equal((await getBooking(db, b.bookingId)).status, "expired", "an ended booking is never resurrected");
  assert.equal((await ticketsOf(db, b.customerId)).length, 4);
});

dbTest("an unknown or malformed id is null and not_found, and the simulation never counts an orphan", async ({ db }) => {
  const before = await orphans(db);
  for (const id of [nanoid(), "../x", "", " ", "a".repeat(65), "p;q", "é"]) {
    assert.equal(await mockCheckoutState(db, id), null, JSON.stringify(id));
    assert.deepEqual(await mockPay(db, id, new Date()), { kind: "not_found" }, JSON.stringify(id));
  }
  assert.equal(await orphans(db), before);
});

dbTest("tenancy: another pro's simulated purchase is paid within its own pro, redirects to its own page, and leaves this pro untouched (S6)", async ({ db, pro }) => {
  const mine = await shop(db, pro);
  const other = await createTestPro(db);
  try {
    const theirs = await buyBook(db, other);
    const state = await mockCheckoutState(db, theirs.purchaseId);
    assert.ok(state?.kind === "pending");
    assert.equal(state.view.cancelPath, `/${other.slug}/seance/${theirs.occurrenceId}?paiement=annule&p=${theirs.purchaseId}`);
    assert.equal(state.view.businessName, await businessNameOf(db, other));

    const res = await mockPay(db, theirs.purchaseId, new Date());
    assert.ok(res.kind === "paid");
    assert.equal(res.merciPath, `/${other.slug}/merci?p=${theirs.purchaseId}`, "never the page of another pro");
    assert.equal((await ticketsOf(db, theirs.customerId)).length, 4);

    assert.equal((await purchaseRow(db, mine.purchaseId)).status, "pending");
    assert.equal((await ticketsOf(db, mine.customerId)).length, 0);
  } finally {
    await deleteTestUser(db, other.userId);
  }
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create `src/lib/same-origin.ts`**

```ts
/**
 * Origin check for route handlers. Next.js compares `Origin` with `Host` for
 * Server Actions only; a route handler gets no such check, so the POST routes
 * that change state (the mock checkout, the personal-link confirmation) do it
 * themselves. Pure: no env, no request object.
 */

/** Origin header equals new URL(appUrl).origin (route handlers get no automatic origin check); null, "null" or a malformed appUrl → false. */
export function sameOrigin(originHeader: string | null, appUrl: string): boolean {
  if (originHeader === null || originHeader === "" || originHeader === "null") return false;
  let expected: string;
  try {
    expected = new URL(appUrl).origin;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
  // An opaque URL (data:, file:) serialises its origin as "null": never a match.
  if (expected === "null") return false;
  // A browser sends the serialised origin (lower case, no path, no trailing slash): anything else is not a browser's.
  return originHeader === expected;
}
```

```ts
/**
 * The simulated checkout (spec E10 « route simulée », L1145-1147, contract
 * § 3.13): what stands in for Stripe Checkout while no Stripe key is set. A
 * GET shows a page and writes nothing; a same-origin POST pays; both only for
 * SIMULATED sessions (checkout_session_id null or `mock_<id>`, SEC-M3), so the
 * mock can never settle a purchase opened against Stripe. No redirect
 * parameter anywhere: the way back is /{slug of the purchase's own pro}/merci.
 * No `server-only`, no env, no process db: the route passes `db`.
 */
import { and, eq } from "drizzle-orm";

import { fulfillPurchase } from "@/lib/booking/fulfillment";
import type { Effect } from "@/lib/booking/types";
import type { Db } from "@/lib/db/atomic";
import { booking, event, occurrence, professional, ticketPurchase, ticketType } from "@/lib/db/schema";
import { escapeHtml } from "@/lib/email-layout";
import { cancelPathOf, isMockSession } from "@/lib/payments/checkout";
import { COPY } from "@/lib/public/messages";
import { isReferenceId } from "@/lib/public/purchase-reads";
import { formatMoney } from "@/lib/utils";

export type MockCheckoutView = {
  purchaseId: string;
  businessName: string;
  productLabel: string;
  amountLabel: string;
  cancelPath: string;
};

/** The cancel link of the simulated page: the séance of a buy + book, else the offer of a shop purchase, else the pro's page. */
export function mockCancelPath(p: {
  slug: string;
  purchaseId: string;
  occurrenceId: string | null;
  offerId: string | null;
}): string {
  if (p.occurrenceId) {
    return cancelPathOf({ kind: "buybook", slug: p.slug, purchaseId: p.purchaseId, occurrenceId: p.occurrenceId });
  }
  if (p.offerId) return cancelPathOf({ kind: "shop", slug: p.slug, purchaseId: p.purchaseId, offerId: p.offerId });
  return `/${p.slug}`;
}

const merciPathOf = (slug: string, purchaseId: string): string => `/${slug}/merci?p=${purchaseId}`;

/** The purchase when its id has the right shape and its session is simulated (null or a mock id); null otherwise, whatever its status. */
async function simulatedPurchase(db: Db, purchaseId: string) {
  if (!isReferenceId(purchaseId)) return null;
  const [row] = await db
    .select({
      purchaseId: ticketPurchase.id,
      status: ticketPurchase.status,
      checkoutSessionId: ticketPurchase.checkoutSessionId,
      label: ticketPurchase.label,
      amountCents: ticketPurchase.amountCents,
      currency: ticketPurchase.currency,
      offerId: ticketPurchase.offerId,
      ticketTypeName: ticketType.name,
      slug: professional.slug,
      businessName: professional.businessName,
      occurrenceId: booking.occurrenceId,
      eventTitle: event.title,
    })
    .from(ticketPurchase)
    .innerJoin(professional, eq(professional.id, ticketPurchase.professionalId))
    .innerJoin(ticketType, eq(ticketType.id, ticketPurchase.ticketTypeId))
    .leftJoin(
      booking,
      and(eq(booking.purchaseId, ticketPurchase.id), eq(booking.professionalId, ticketPurchase.professionalId)),
    )
    .leftJoin(occurrence, eq(occurrence.id, booking.occurrenceId))
    .leftJoin(event, eq(event.id, occurrence.eventId))
    .where(eq(ticketPurchase.id, purchaseId));
  if (!row) return null;
  if (row.checkoutSessionId !== null && !isMockSession(row.checkoutSessionId)) return null;
  return row;
}

/** GET of the simulated checkout (no write): a pending purchase whose checkout_session_id is null or a mock id → its view; a paid one → its merci path; else null (a purchase opened against Stripe is never shown here, SEC-M3). */
export async function mockCheckoutState(
  db: Db,
  purchaseId: string,
): Promise<{ kind: "pending"; view: MockCheckoutView } | { kind: "paid"; merciPath: string } | null> {
  const p = await simulatedPurchase(db, purchaseId);
  if (!p) return null;
  if (p.status === "paid") return { kind: "paid", merciPath: merciPathOf(p.slug, p.purchaseId) };
  if (p.status !== "pending") return null;
  return {
    kind: "pending",
    view: {
      purchaseId: p.purchaseId,
      businessName: p.businessName,
      productLabel: `${p.eventTitle ?? p.ticketTypeName} · ${p.label}`,
      amountLabel: formatMoney(p.amountCents, p.currency),
      cancelPath: mockCancelPath({
        slug: p.slug,
        purchaseId: p.purchaseId,
        occurrenceId: p.occurrenceId,
        offerId: p.offerId,
      }),
    },
  };
}

export type MockPayResult = { kind: "paid"; merciPath: string; effects: Effect[] } | { kind: "not_found" };

/** POST: only a purchase whose checkout_session_id is null or isMockSession (SEC-M3, « the mock pays only simulated sessions »): fulfillPurchase(db, id, { sessionId: null, paymentIntentId: null, livemode: false }) (L1112); merciPath = /{slug of the purchase's own pro}/merci?p={id} (L1146-1147: no redirect parameter); anything else → not_found. */
export async function mockPay(db: Db, purchaseId: string, now: Date): Promise<MockPayResult> {
  const p = await simulatedPurchase(db, purchaseId);
  if (!p) return { kind: "not_found" };
  const res = await fulfillPurchase(db, p.purchaseId, { sessionId: null, paymentIntentId: null, livemode: false }, now);
  // The purchase vanished between the read and the batch: nothing to pay, and no orphan to count for a simulation.
  if (res.outcome === "orphan") return { kind: "not_found" };
  return { kind: "paid", merciPath: merciPathOf(p.slug, p.purchaseId), effects: res.effects };
}

const STYLE = `
    body { margin: 0; background: #f4f4f5; color: #18181b; font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif; line-height: 1.5; }
    main { box-sizing: border-box; max-width: 28rem; margin: 2rem auto; padding: 1.5rem; background: #fff; border: 1px solid #e4e4e7; border-radius: 1rem; }
    h1 { margin: 0 0 1rem; font-size: 1.25rem; }
    .business { margin: 0; font-weight: 600; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
    .product { margin: 0.25rem 0 0; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
    .amount { margin: 0.25rem 0 1rem; font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 700; }
    .note { margin: 0 0 1.25rem; padding: 0.75rem; background: #fffbeb; border: 1px solid #fcd34d; border-radius: 0.5rem; color: #78350f; font-size: 0.875rem; }
    button { font: inherit; font-weight: 600; padding: 0.75rem 1.25rem; color: #fff; background: #4f46e5; border: 0; border-radius: 0.625rem; cursor: pointer; }
    button:focus-visible, a:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #1d4ed8; outline-offset: 2px; }
    a { color: #4338ca; }
    .back { margin: 1rem 0 0; }
    @media (max-width: 640px) {
      main { margin: 0; border-radius: 0; border-left: 0; border-right: 0; }
      button { width: 100%; }
    }`;

/** Server-built page « Paiement simulé » (exact copy below); every value escaped; no script; the form POSTs to /api/mock-checkout. */
export function mockCheckoutHtml(view: MockCheckoutView): string {
  const e = escapeHtml;
  return `<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<meta name="robots" content="noindex">
<meta name="referrer" content="strict-origin">
<title>Paiement simulé</title>
<style>${STYLE}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<main>
  <h1>Paiement simulé</h1>
  <p class="business">${e(view.businessName)}</p>
  <p class="product">${e(view.productLabel)}</p>
  <p class="amount">${e(view.amountLabel)}</p>
  <p class="note">${e(COPY.PAYMENTS_TEST_MOCK)}</p>
  <form method="post" action="/api/mock-checkout">
    <input type="hidden" name="purchase" value="${e(view.purchaseId)}">
    <button type="submit">Payer (simulation)</button>
  </form>
  <p class="back"><a href="${e(view.cancelPath)}">Annuler et revenir</a></p>
</main>
</body>
</html>`;
}
```

Note on the mobile rule: the `STYLE` text holds `button { width: 100%; }` on its own line inside the `@media (max-width: 640px)` block, which is the last rule of the sheet; the third pure test slices the page from that media rule and checks the button rule in it.

```ts
// The route handler imports next/server, which node:test cannot load: its wiring is pinned on the source.
const ROUTE = readFileSync("src/app/api/mock-checkout/route.ts", "utf8");

/** The text of `export async function <verb>(` up to the next doc comment or exported function (or the end of the file). */
function bodyOf(verb: "GET" | "POST"): string {
  const start = ROUTE.indexOf(`export async function ${verb}(`);
  assert.notEqual(start, -1, `${verb} is exported`);
  const ends = [ROUTE.indexOf("\n/**", start + 1), ROUTE.indexOf("\nexport async function", start + 1)].filter((i) => i !== -1);
  return ROUTE.slice(start, ends.length === 0 ? undefined : Math.min(...ends));
}
```

```ts
import { after } from "next/server";

import { db } from "@/lib/db";
import { env } from "@/lib/env";
import { mockCheckoutHtml, mockCheckoutState, mockPay } from "@/lib/payments/mock-checkout";
import { isReferenceId } from "@/lib/public/purchase-reads";
import { sameOrigin } from "@/lib/same-origin";
import { mockCheckoutEnabled } from "@/lib/stripe";
import { runEffects } from "@/server/notify";

export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";

/**
 * Every response: not cached, not framed, the origin alone as referrer (SEC-M11); the page is built by the server and the
 * route has no other output. `strict-origin`, not `no-referrer`: the policy of the document that holds the form also decides
 * the `Origin` header of its POST, and `no-referrer` makes browsers send `Origin: null`, which `sameOrigin` must refuse.
 */
const HEADERS = {
  "Cache-Control": "no-store",
  "Content-Security-Policy": "frame-ancestors 'none'",
  "X-Frame-Options": "DENY",
  "Referrer-Policy": "strict-origin",
} as const;

function notFound(): Response {
  return new Response("Not found", { status: 404, headers: { ...HEADERS } });
}

/** 303 to a path of this app: built from the trusted app URL, never from the request. */
function seeOther(path: string): Response {
  return new Response(null, { status: 303, headers: { ...HEADERS, Location: new URL(path, env.APP_URL).toString() } });
}

/**
 * Simulated Stripe Checkout, GET (spec E10, contract § 3.13). Available only
 * when mockCheckoutEnabled() (no Stripe keys, not production by APP_ENV nor
 * VERCEL_ENV): 404 everywhere else. Shows the page of a pending simulated
 * purchase and writes nothing, so a prefetcher or a link scanner can never pay
 * (L1847); a paid one goes on to its merci page; anything else is a 404. The
 * only parameter is `purchase`: there is no redirect parameter.
 */
export async function GET(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  if (!mockCheckoutEnabled()) return notFound();
  const purchaseId = new URL(request.url).searchParams.get("purchase");
  if (!isReferenceId(purchaseId)) return notFound();
  const state = await mockCheckoutState(db, purchaseId);
  if (!state) return notFound();
  if (state.kind === "paid") return seeOther(state.merciPath);
  return new Response(mockCheckoutHtml(state.view), {
    status: 200,
    headers: { ...HEADERS, "Content-Type": "text/html; charset=utf-8" },
  });
}

/**
 * Simulated Stripe Checkout, POST: « Payer (simulation) ». A route handler
 * gets no automatic Origin check, so it is made here before the body is read
 * (403). The purchase id comes from the form field `purchase` only; the engine
 * fulfils it for a simulated session and the effects run after the response
 * with the budget "none" (Decision 74). 303 to the merci page of the
 * purchase's own pro.
 */
export async function POST(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  if (!mockCheckoutEnabled()) return notFound();
  if (!sameOrigin(request.headers.get("origin"), env.APP_URL)) {
    return new Response("Forbidden", { status: 403, headers: { ...HEADERS } });
  }
  let purchaseId: unknown = null;
  try {
    purchaseId = (await request.formData()).get("purchase");
  } catch {
    return notFound();
  }
  if (!isReferenceId(purchaseId)) return notFound();
  const res = await mockPay(db, purchaseId, new Date());
  if (res.kind === "not_found") return notFound();
  const effects = res.effects;
  if (effects.length > 0) after(() => runEffects(effects, "none"));
  return seeOther(res.merciPath);
}
```

```ts
// src/lib/cron-auth.ts (pure, node:crypto)
export const CRON_SECRET_MIN_LENGTH = 32;
/** True only for exactly `Bearer <secret>` with a secret of at least CRON_SECRET_MIN_LENGTH characters (SEC-M5), compared in constant time (sha256 digests + timingSafeEqual). */
export function cronAuthorized(authorization: string | null, secret: string | undefined): boolean;

// src/lib/env-checks.ts (pure, SEC-I5, SEC-M5)
/** Boot refusals, in this order: VERCEL_ENV "production" with APP_ENV not "production" → "APP_ENV must be production on a Vercel production deployment"; APP_ENV "production" with BETTER_AUTH_SECRET under 32 characters → "BETTER_AUTH_SECRET must be at least 32 characters in production". [] when none. */
export function envBootErrors(raw: { VERCEL_ENV?: string; APP_ENV: string; BETTER_AUTH_SECRET: string }): string[];

// src/app/api/cron/daily/route.ts
export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";
export const maxDuration = 300;
export async function GET(request: Request): Promise<Response>;

// src/lib/booking/nightly.ts (engine change)
export async function ensureAllHorizons(
  db: Db,
  now: Date = new Date(),
  opts: { ensure?: typeof ensureHorizon; deadline?: number } = {}, // test-only ensure; deadline = epoch ms, default Date.now() + 120_000
): Promise<{ pros: number; inserted: number; failures: string[] }>;
// addition of this task (test-only, not in § 3.14): the way a test reaches step 4 of runNightly
export async function runNightly(db: Db, now?: Date, opts?: { horizon?: Parameters<typeof ensureAllHorizons>[2] }): Promise<NightlyReport>;

// src/lib/env.ts
// env.CRON_SECRET: string | undefined (schema: z.string().optional()); env.CRON_CONFIGURED: boolean
```

Design notes (read before coding):
- `/api/cron/daily` is called by Vercel Cron with `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>` (Vercel sends it when the project has a `CRON_SECRET` variable). It answers 401 « Unauthorized » when the secret is unset, shorter than 32 characters or different, compared in constant time on two sha256 digests (so two headers of different length never throw and never leak the length through timing).
- The route returns counts only (no id, no e-mail); `errors[]` of the report is authoritative: 200 when empty, 500 otherwise, each entry logged once as `[cron] <logSafeMessage>`.
- Contradiction found and settled: the contract writes `logSafeMessage(e)` for each `report.errors` entry, but those entries are strings and `logSafeMessage` of a bare string answers `unknown error` (it reads `message` of an Error or an object). The route passes `logSafeMessage({ message: entry })`, the same form `src/server/notify.ts` uses for the budget line, so the address-masking still applies and the text is kept.
- `ensureAllHorizons` (OUT:126): each pro runs in its own `try`; a throw or an `ok: false` becomes a `failures` entry (`pro <id>: <message or code>`) and the next pro still runs; before every pro after the first, `Date.now() > deadline` stops the loop with `deadline reached after <n> pro(s)` so a slow step 4 cannot starve steps 5 to 7 within `maxDuration`. The old direct `console.error` of the engine goes: `failures` reach `report.errors` and the route logs them once.
- Boot checks: `env.ts` throws at import when a Vercel production deployment runs with `APP_ENV` other than `production` (the mock checkout and the mock mail key off it) or when production has a `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` under 32 characters. A local build has no `VERCEL_ENV`. The Resend refusal is not repeated (`src/lib/email.ts` already refuses a production without a key).
- `CRON_SECRET` is optional in the schema: a missing or placeholder secret makes `env.CRON_CONFIGURED` false and the route 401, never a boot failure.
- Task 1 removed the dashes of `src/lib/booking/nightly.ts` and `vercel.ts` (comments included): the Edits below anchor on lines that contain none.

**Security tests owned here (contract § 8.4):**
- S15 (boot part): `env-checks.test.ts` (production on Vercel needs `APP_ENV` production; production needs a secret of 32 characters).
- S17: `cron-auth.test.ts` (the matrix: the exact bearer of a 32-character secret, a 31-character secret refused, wrong secret, missing header, lower-case scheme, extra space, empty or undefined secret) and the curl of the browser step (401).
- S49 (cron): `cron-auth.test.ts` route guard (the route runs no effect, so no budget is chosen; were a later step to return some, they would run with `"none"`).
- S31 (cron): `cron-auth.test.ts` route guard (`logSafeMessage`, no raw `err` passed to `console.*`).

```ts
test("CRON_SECRET_MIN_LENGTH is 32 and the fixture secret has exactly that length", () => {
  assert.equal(CRON_SECRET_MIN_LENGTH, 32);
  assert.equal(SECRET.length, 32);

test("cronAuthorized: exactly `Bearer <secret>` of a secret of 32 characters or more is accepted", () => {

  const long = "k".repeat(64);
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(`Bearer ${long}`, long), true);
});

test("cronAuthorized: a secret shorter than 32 characters never authorizes, even with the exact header (SEC-M5)", () => {
  const short = SECRET.slice(0, 31);
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(`Bearer ${short}`, short), false);

test("cronAuthorized: a wrong secret, a missing header and every variant of the scheme are refused", () => {
  const other = "f".repeat(32);
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(`Bearer ${other}`, SECRET), false, "wrong secret");
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(`Bearer ${SECRET.slice(0, 31)}`, SECRET), false, "a prefix of the secret");
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(`Bearer ${SECRET}x`, SECRET), false, "the secret and one more character");
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(null, SECRET), false, "no header");
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized("", SECRET), false, "empty header");
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(`bearer ${SECRET}`, SECRET), false, "lower-case scheme");
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(`BEARER ${SECRET}`, SECRET), false, "upper-case scheme");
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(`Bearer  ${SECRET}`, SECRET), false, "two spaces");
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(` Bearer ${SECRET}`, SECRET), false, "leading space");
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(`Bearer ${SECRET} `, SECRET), false, "trailing space");
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(`Bearer\t${SECRET}`, SECRET), false, "a tab");
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(SECRET, SECRET), false, "the secret without its scheme");
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(`Basic ${SECRET}`, SECRET), false, "another scheme");
});

test("cronAuthorized: an unset, empty or blank secret authorizes nothing, not even an empty bearer", () => {
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(`Bearer ${SECRET}`, undefined), false);
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(`Bearer ${SECRET}`, ""), false);
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized("Bearer ", ""), false);
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized("Bearer ", undefined), false);
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(null, undefined), false);
  const blank = " ".repeat(32);
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(`Bearer ${blank}`, blank), false, "a blank secret of 32 spaces");
});

test("cronAuthorized: a header of any length is compared without throwing", () => {
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized("x".repeat(10_000), SECRET), false);
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized("é".repeat(40), SECRET), false);
  assert.equal(cronAuthorized(`Bearer ${SECRET}`, "é".repeat(40)), false);
});

test("cronAuthorized compares sha256 digests with timingSafeEqual, never the strings with ===", () => {
  const source = readFileSync("src/lib/cron-auth.ts", "utf8");
  assert.match(source, /timingSafeEqual\(/);
  assert.match(source, /createHash\("sha256"\)/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(source, /[!=]==\s*`Bearer|`Bearer[^`]*`\s*[!=]==/, "the header is never compared as a string");
});
```

`src/lib/cron-auth.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Bearer check of the nightly job (spec E12, L1184-1185). Vercel Cron sends
 * `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>` when the project has that variable;
 * the route refuses everything else. Pure: no env, no request object.
 */
import { createHash, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

/** A cron secret shorter than this is refused (SEC-M5): the route stays closed until the owner sets a long one. */
export const CRON_SECRET_MIN_LENGTH = 32;

/** sha256 of a string: two digests always have the same length, so timingSafeEqual never throws and never leaks the length. */
const digest = (value: string): Buffer => createHash("sha256").update(value, "utf8").digest();

/** True only for exactly `Bearer <secret>` with a secret of at least CRON_SECRET_MIN_LENGTH characters (SEC-M5), compared in constant time (sha256 digests + timingSafeEqual). */
export function cronAuthorized(authorization: string | null, secret: string | undefined): boolean {
  if (secret === undefined || secret.trim().length < CRON_SECRET_MIN_LENGTH) return false;
  if (authorization === null) return false;
  return timingSafeEqual(digest(authorization), digest(`Bearer ${secret}`));
}
```

`src/lib/env-checks.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Boot refusals of the environment (SEC-I5, SEC-M5), kept apart from env.ts so
 * they are tested without loading it (env.ts reads process.env at import).
 * Pure: no env, no I/O.
 */

const BETTER_AUTH_SECRET_MIN_LENGTH = 32;

/** Boot refusals, in this order: VERCEL_ENV "production" with APP_ENV not "production" → "APP_ENV must be production on a Vercel production deployment"; APP_ENV "production" with BETTER_AUTH_SECRET under 32 characters → "BETTER_AUTH_SECRET must be at least 32 characters in production". [] when none. */
export function envBootErrors(raw: { VERCEL_ENV?: string; APP_ENV: string; BETTER_AUTH_SECRET: string }): string[] {
  const errors: string[] = [];
  if (raw.VERCEL_ENV === "production" && raw.APP_ENV !== "production") {
    errors.push("APP_ENV must be production on a Vercel production deployment");
  }
  if (raw.APP_ENV === "production" && raw.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET.length < BETTER_AUTH_SECRET_MIN_LENGTH) {
    errors.push("BETTER_AUTH_SECRET must be at least 32 characters in production");
  }
  return errors;
}
```

```ts
  const other = await twoProsWithEvents(db, pro);

    const seen: string[] = [];
    // The first pro of the night throws, whoever it is (the shared branch may hold other runs' pros); our two pros
    // answer not ok when they are not that first one; every other pro is done at once.
    const ensure: EnsureFn = async (_db, proId) => {
      seen.push(proId);
      if (seen.length === 1) throw new Error("boom");
      if (proId === pro.proId || proId === other.proId) return { ok: false, code: "stale" };
      return { ok: true, effects: [], inserted: 0, complete: true };
    };
    const res = await ensureAllHorizons(db, new Date(), { ensure, deadline: Date.now() + 600_000 });
    const [first] = seen;
    assert.equal(seen.length, res.pros, "every pro was started once: a throwing pro never stops the night");
    assert.ok(seen.includes(pro.proId) && seen.includes(other.proId), "both pros were tried, whatever their order");
    assert.equal(res.failures[0], `pro ${first}: boom`, "the first pro is named with its error");
    const notFirst = [pro.proId, other.proId].filter((id) => id !== first);
    assert.ok(notFirst.length >= 1);
    for (const id of notFirst) assert.ok(res.failures.includes(`pro ${id}: stale`), JSON.stringify(res.failures));
    assert.equal(res.inserted, 0);
    assert.ok(res.pros >= 2);

    await deleteTestUser(db, other.userId);
  }
});
```

```
/** Step 4: ensureHorizon for every pro with a non-archived event, looping while incomplete (≤ HORIZON_CALLS_PER_PRO calls). */
export async function ensureAllHorizons(db: Db, now: Date = new Date()): Promise<{ pros: number; inserted: number }> {

    .selectDistinct({ id: event.professionalId })
    .from(event)
    .where(isNull(event.archivedAt))

      if (!res.ok) {
```

new_string:
```
/**
 * Step 4: ensureHorizon for every pro with a non-archived event, looping while incomplete (≤ HORIZON_CALLS_PER_PRO calls).
 * Each pro runs in its own `try`: a throw or an `ok: false` is reported in `failures` ("pro <id>: <message or code>") and
 * the next pro still runs. Before every pro after the first, once `deadline` (epoch ms, default now + 120 s) has passed,
 * it stops starting pros and says so (OUT:126). `opts.ensure` and `opts.deadline` are test-only.
 */
export async function ensureAllHorizons(
  db: Db,
  now: Date = new Date(),
  opts: { ensure?: typeof ensureHorizon; deadline?: number } = {},
): Promise<{ pros: number; inserted: number; failures: string[] }> {
  const ensure = opts.ensure ?? ensureHorizon;
  const deadline = opts.deadline ?? Date.now() + HORIZON_DEADLINE_MS;
  const pros = await db
    .selectDistinct({ id: event.professionalId })
    .from(event)
    .where(isNull(event.archivedAt))
    .orderBy(asc(event.professionalId));
  let inserted = 0;
  let started = 0;
  const failures: string[] = [];
  for (const { id } of pros) {
    if (started > 0 && Date.now() > deadline) {
      failures.push(`deadline reached after ${started} pro(s)`);
      break;
    }
    started += 1;
    try {
      for (let call = 0; call < HORIZON_CALLS_PER_PRO; call++) {
        const res = await ensure(db, id, now);
        if (!res.ok) {
          failures.push(`pro ${id}: ${res.code}`);
          break;
        }
        inserted += res.inserted;
        if (res.complete) break;
      }
    } catch (err) {
      failures.push(`pro ${id}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`);
    }
  }
  return { pros: pros.length, inserted, failures };
}
```

Create `src/app/api/cron/daily/route.ts`:

```ts
import { runNightly, type NightlyReport } from "@/lib/booking/nightly";
import { cronAuthorized } from "@/lib/cron-auth";
import { db } from "@/lib/db";
import { env } from "@/lib/env";
import { logSafeMessage } from "@/lib/log-safe";

export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";
export const maxDuration = 300;

const NO_STORE = { "Cache-Control": "no-store" } as const;

/**
 * Nightly job (spec E12, contract § 3.14), called by Vercel Cron once a day
 * (`vercel.ts`). 401 « Unauthorized » unless the request carries exactly
 * `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>` with a configured secret of 32
 * characters at least (constant-time comparison); the route then runs the
 * steps and answers counts only, never an id or an address. The `errors` of
 * the report are authoritative: 200 when there is none, 500 otherwise, and
 * each is logged once through logSafeMessage. The job sends no e-mail
 * (OUT:118), so the route runs no effect.
 */
export async function GET(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  const secret = env.CRON_CONFIGURED ? env.CRON_SECRET : undefined;
  if (!cronAuthorized(request.headers.get("authorization"), secret)) {
    return new Response("Unauthorized", { status: 401, headers: NO_STORE });
  }

  let report: NightlyReport;
  try {
    report = await runNightly(db, new Date());
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(`[cron] run failed: ${logSafeMessage(err)}`);
    return Response.json({ ok: false, errors: 1 }, { status: 500, headers: NO_STORE });
  }
  for (const error of report.errors) console.error(`[cron] ${logSafeMessage({ message: error })}`);

  const ok = report.errors.length === 0;
  return Response.json(
    {
      ok,
      expiredBookings: report.expiredBookings,
      expiredPurchases: report.expiredPurchases,
      expiredTickets: report.expiredTickets,
      horizonPros: report.horizon.pros,
      horizonInserted: report.horizon.inserted,
      archivedEvents: report.archivedEvents,
      purgedThrottle: report.purgedThrottle,
      invariantViolations: report.invariantViolations,
      errors: report.errors.length,
    },
    { status: ok ? 200 : 500, headers: NO_STORE },
  );
}
```
